clue.text: Quick sauce containing radish top

indicators.note: containing means the sauce holds the radish letter within it

parts.note: pesto is the Italian basil sauce

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so only the start of radish is used

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: a speedy sauce with a bit of radish thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction for a fast tempo, so it means quick.

clue.text: Child in charge of rising currency

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the short word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: of can show responsibility, as in a minister of health, one in charge of health
sterling is the British currency

explanation.surface: A child running a currency that is going up in value.
explanation.definitionFit: A fosterling is a foster child, one brought up by people other than its parents.

clue.text: Given beers, cur turns to Hound of Hades

indicators.note: the cur supposedly turns into something else, so the letters of the two words are recast

explanation.surface: A mongrel plied with beer becomes the monstrous dog of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Cerberus is the many-headed watchdog guarding the gates of the underworld.

clue.text: Abandon waste

definitions.meaning: to leave someone or something behind, as a soldier leaves his post
a barren wasteland such as the Sahara

explanation.surface: Leave behind a barren land.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to abandon; as a noun, a barren wilderness.

clue.text: Abstemious Dickensian accepted for dull work

indicators.note: accepted means the abstemious word takes in the Dickens name

parts.note: dry describes someone who abstains from alcohol
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A teetotal character from Dickens taking on tedious labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of Dickens's novel of the Gordon Riots.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, menial and monotonous labour.

clue.text: Resounding end of pointless missile

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the tail of pointless is used

parts.note: Trident is the submarine-launched nuclear missile system

explanation.surface: A loud warning that a nuclear missile is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident sound is loud and harsh, ringing out.

clue.text: Deaf hero's wrinkled brow

indicators.note: something wrinkled is creased out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deaf hero has a furrowed brow.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow is the part of the face above the eyes, another word for it.

clue.text: Kind of mess only some care to notice

indicators.note: only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Few people bother to see a certain sort of mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton mess is an English dessert of strawberries, cream and broken meringue, named after the school.

clue.text: Shiny-nosed character is sound as a bell

definitions.meaning: Edward Lear's nonsense poem tells of the creature with a luminous nose
the deep noise a bell makes when struck

explanation.surface: A character with a shiny nose is perfectly healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy; it is the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's poem 'The Dong with a Luminous Nose' names this creature; the word is also a bell's peal.

clue.text: Disquiet caused by right tunes in wrong order

indicators.note: the letters are placed in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Discontent over the right songs being played out of sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is public disquiet or agitation.

clue.text: Obstinate remnant brought to light

parts.note: a stub is what is left, as of a pencil or cigarette
a baby born is brought into the light of the world

explanation.surface: A stubborn leftover finally uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn people are obstinate, refusing to change their minds.

clue.text: Highly sexed person keeping Dan Brown's sources distinct from 18?

indicators.note: keeping means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: a goer is slang for a sexually active person

indicators.note: the sources of the words are their opening letters

parts.note: other than means distinct from

explanation.surface: A lustful character in a Dan Brown thriller, set apart from the religious types.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 18-across, EVANGELICAL; the question mark flags the jokey slang. 'Goer' is British slang for someone keen on sex.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for a person who preaches religion zealously, a pushy evangelist.

clue.text: Bear bearing part of ship — and a lot of noise

indicators.note: in a down clue the bear carries the other pieces above it

parts.note: the hull is the main body of a ship
Baloo is the bear in The Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A bear carrying a chunk of ship makes a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is an uproar, a commotion with much noise.

clue.text: Attractive female's artwork

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female; the 's is a link meaning is
an etching is a print made from an engraved plate

explanation.surface: A woman's artwork is lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching means attractive, charming in appearance.

clue.text: Sporty sort of Greek hosting heads of Hungary, Latvia and Estonia

indicators.note: hosting means the Greek word holds the initials inside it

parts.note: Attic is the ancient Greek dialect of Athens

indicators.note: the heads of the countries are their first letters

explanation.surface: A sporting Greek welcoming the leaders of three European nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Attic, the dialect and culture of ancient Athens, is the sort of Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic means fit and good at sport.

clue.text: Novel interrupting genuine fresh start

indicators.note: interrupting means the novel word breaks into the genuine one

parts.note: genuine means real
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: A book that breaks up an authentic new beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal is a revival or beginning again, a fresh start.

clue.text: Shakespeare's beloved worship uplifted in any place

parts.note: the Sonnets are dedicated to the mysterious Mr W.H.

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to revere is to worship

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's beloved is adored and praised wherever they go.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherever means in whatever place, anywhere.

clue.text: Scrutinise bug, keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the bug holds the quiet letter inside it

parts.note: a bug is an insect
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: Examining a bug while staying silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, to scrutinise.

clue.text: Guardian, say, interrupting Alice 5, peculiarly missionary

indicators.note: interrupting means the five and the guardian break into the jumbled name
peculiarly signals the letters are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
a guardian angel is one example

explanation.surface: A newspaper wedged oddly into Alice's tale, crusading for a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiarly' rearranges ALICE as EICAL, and 'interrupting' puts V and ANGEL in after its E. Guardian is a newspaper in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelical person is zealous about spreading a faith, missionary in spirit.

clue.text: Bait to entrap holy person's sheen

indicators.note: entrap means the bait catches the holy letters inside it

parts.note: a lure is bait
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Using bait to ensnare a saint's radiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a gentle shine or gloss on a surface.

clue.text: Composer's endless component of salad

indicators.note: read as end-less, the salad word loses the letters spelling end

parts.note: endives are salad leaves

explanation.surface: A composer's salad ingredient with no end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' reads as 'end less': take END from ENDIVES. The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer.

clue.text: Man maybe somewhat misleading

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A man who is a bit deceptive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Irrational Southern church extremely popular outside

indicators.note: outside means the popular word sits around the southern church letters

parts.note: something viral spreads fast online, hugely popular
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A southern church whose extreme popularity is beyond reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Visceral feelings come from the gut rather than reasoning, so they are irrational.

clue.text: Help string player losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a bassist plays the double bass or bass guitar

explanation.surface: A musician who has lost their head and needs help.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to assist someone is to give them a hand or aid.

clue.text: Carelessly lost knee bones

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters end up out of place

explanation.surface: Someone carelessly lost knee bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the full framework of bones in a body.

clue.text: Unfortunate habit involving piece of music

indicators.note: involving means the habit takes in the music

parts.note: a tic is a habitual twitch or quirk
a rag is a ragtime piece

explanation.surface: A sad habit of playing a certain tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means dreadfully unfortunate.
